rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for something that naturally belongs to or follows from something else.

example.english: The hardship of working night shifts is inherent; you’ll know after doing it for a while.
example.traditional: 夜更返工本身有嘅辛苦，做耐咗就知喇。
example.jyutping: je6 gaang1 faan1 gung1 bun2 san1 jau5 ge3 san1 fu2 zou6 noi6 zo2 zau6 zi1 laa3

rows.note: Use this more formal term when describing an intrinsic or built-in quality, especially in careful or written language.

example.english: This system has inherent limitations, so it cannot be applied indiscriminately.
example.traditional: 呢套制度存在固有嘅限制，唔可以一刀切。
example.jyutping: ni1 tou3 zai3 dou6 cyun4 zoi6 gu3 jau5 ge3 haan6 zai3 m4 ho2 ji5 jat1 dou1 cit3

rows.note: Use this when the inherent quality is an inner or intrinsic feature rather than an outward or added one.

example.english: Confidence isn’t something you can put on; it is an inherent strength within a person.
example.traditional: 自信唔係扮出嚟嘅，而係一個人內在嘅力量。
example.jyutping: zi6 seon3 m4 hai6 baan6 ceot1 lai4 ge3 ji4 hai6 jat1 go3 jan4 noi6 zoi6 ge3 lik6 loeng6
